title: California Proposition 45 and Data Center Concerns
excerpt: Environmental advocates warn that California's Proposition 45 could create a loophole allowing data centers to bypass public and environmental scrutiny.
body_html:
A California ballot measure, Proposition 45, is facing criticism from environmental advocates who warn it may contain a loophole for data center developers. The initiative is pitched as a way to speed up the development of essential infrastructure.

If passed, the proposition would shorten the timelines required for state-mandated environmental reviews for eligible projects. Additionally, it would introduce obstacles that make it harder for local residents to challenge these developments in court.

Advocates are concerned that these proposed changes could allow data center projects to evade standard public scrutiny and environmental evaluations. Proponents of the measure argue it serves as a fast track for critical infrastructure needs, but critics highlight the potential risks regarding transparency and environmental oversight.
